clue.text: Completely lose one's grip

parts.note: reads like a tool whose head parts company with its shaft, but the phrase means to lose one's temper

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose self-control suddenly in anger, a complete loss of one's grip on composure.

clue.text: Chapter head's wood?

parts.note: the head of a cathedral chapter is its dean, so a wood belonging to him would be named after his title

explanation.surface: A question about woodland owned by the senior cleric of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathedral chapter is headed by a dean; the Forest of Dean is an ancient woodland in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This English royal forest in Gloucestershire is a famous wood whose name happens to be a cleric's title.

clue.text: Buyer banned inclusion of tea

indicators.note: the letters wanted are included within the two words that follow, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A purchaser is prohibited from taking a hot drink with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American infusion, also called maté, is drunk as a tea.

clue.text: Ron with effort removed cutting edge

indicators.note: the letters of the name and the noun are moved away from their order and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ron has made an effort that was taken away from him on the leading edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges RON plus EFFORT; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the cutting edge means being in the foremost, most advanced position.

clue.text: Teresa goes about the work left in a revealing way

indicators.note: the short form of the woman's name travels around the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: Tess is a pet form of the name Teresa
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A woman named Teresa walks round the building where she works, dressed provocatively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is just a link before 'work'; 'goes about' makes the woman's pet name surround the two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Going without a top exposes the upper body, so dressing that way is revealing.

clue.text: Purple ruler

parts.note: purple is the colour of imperial robes, and it also names a British butterfly, so a monarch of the highest rank is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Purple dye was reserved for Roman sovereigns of empires, and the Purple Emperor is a butterfly.

clue.text: Wrestling — everybody available

definitions.meaning: ... wrestling is a freestyle form of the sport with few restrictions
if all are in, every person is present and ready

explanation.definitionFit: All-in is a no-holds-barred kind of grappling, and the phrase also means that every person is included.

clue.text: Diminutive lady's price for unloading

parts.note: Di, a short form of Diana, plus the possessive 's
a charge is the price asked for something

explanation.surface: A small woman pays a fee when she unloads her goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' signals the shortened name DI, not a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge cargo is to unload it from a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Less common recipes are accepted

indicators.note: the pair of letters takes in the word that follows, holding it between them

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions, so two of them give RR
taken as written

explanation.surface: Unusual recipes find approval in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer occurs less often, so it is more uncommon.

clue.text: Father's socially acceptable catalogue appealing to the mass of the people

definitions.text: appealing to the mass of the people

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: Dad keeps a respectable inventory designed to please the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist politician or policy aims at the wishes of ordinary voters.

clue.text: Bilingual finish

parts.note: a finish named after two languages spoken by Europeans, which is in fact a glossy shellac coating for wood

explanation.definitionFit: This shellac technique gives furniture a high-gloss finish, and its name joins two nationalities' languages.

clue.text: Pinch a bit

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to steal something small
a horse's bit with a jointed mouthpiece is one kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to take without permission, and it also names a simple jointed bit used on horses.

clue.text: Farmer hurried, despite having resistance, to trap revolutionary

indicators.note: the outer pieces catch the revolutionary inside them

parts.note: ran means hurried
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A farmer rushed, though faced with opposition, to catch a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'despite having' is padding for the surface; 'to trap' signals that the revolutionary sits inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a cattle ranch is a kind of farmer.

clue.text: Loves to go round middle of stage in new Zealand

indicators.note: the two round letters circle the central part of the following word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves give OO

indicators.note: the letters between the first and last of the word stage

explanation.surface: Sweethearts set off around the centre of a stage in a New Zealand theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes all but the first and last letters of 'stage'; 'to go round' wraps the two loves around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of the South Island, so it lies in that country.

clue.text: A student with two graduates three times at school

parts.note: L is a learner, as on the L-plate

indicators.note: the degree abbreviation is taken twice, once for each graduate

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
ter is Latin for three times

explanation.surface: One student accompanied by a pair of graduates appears three times at the school.
explanation.walkthrough: TER is Latin for 'thrice', a word music and pharmacy still use.
explanation.definitionFit: One's alma mater is the school or university one attended.

clue.text: Discard club found in junkyard

parts.note: to scrap is to throw away
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a golf club they came across in a junkyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste metal of this kind is the typical stock of a scrapyard.

clue.text: Three maps mistakenly taken from overcoat

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put together in the wrong order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone took three maps from a coat by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken from' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A petersham is a heavy overcoat named after Viscount Petersham, as well as a ribbon.

clue.text: Missed tea coming out of coffee cup

indicators.note: the letters of these words emerge in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Somebody missed their tea pouring out of a coffee cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup used for strong black coffee.

clue.text: To dispose of cheaply by the redistribution of fells

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow are shared out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting rid of hillside land cheaply by dividing up the fells.
explanation.walkthrough: Fells are hills in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell off goods is to get rid of them, usually at a reduced price.

clue.text: He spelt different lady's name

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are made into something different

explanation.surface: A man wrote a woman's name in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Elspeth is a Scottish form of the girl's name Elizabeth.

clue.text: Backbiters?

parts.note: taken literally, those at the back of the mouth that bite, rather than people who speak ill of others

explanation.definitionFit: Molars and other rear dentition literally bite at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Officer's colourful butterfly

definitions.meaning: the highest rank of naval commander
the red ... and white ... are bright butterflies

explanation.definitionFit: The title is a senior naval rank and also the name of a brightly marked butterfly.

clue.text: Like trees that have been replanted

definitions.text: Like trees that have been replanted

indicators.note: the word trees has its letters planted again in a new order

explanation.surface: Describing woodland saplings put into new ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer; replanted trees have been set again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a plant again in the soil is to put it back in place, hence replanted.

clue.text: In southern Europe it comes as a hot dusty blow

definitions.text: In southern Europe it comes as a hot dusty blow

parts.words: In southern Europe it comes as a hot dusty blow
parts.note: a blow sounds like a punch, but here it is a gust of wind from North Africa

explanation.surface: Something reaches Mediterranean countries as a hot, dusty punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot, dust-laden wind blowing from the Sahara into southern Europe.

clue.text: Church has one vessel or another

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church owns a vessel of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'another' (vessel): a butter churn is a second kind of vessel. 'has' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A churn is a container for making butter or carrying milk, so a different kind of receptacle.

clue.text: To cope so clumsily with medical instrument

indicators.note: the letters of these words are handled awkwardly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Struggling to handle a doctor's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors use an otoscope to look inside the ear.

clue.text: Time I have for alluring woman

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

explanation.surface: A seductress makes time for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is a beautiful maiden of Islamic paradise, hence any voluptuous beauty.

clue.text: One appearing on the calendar

parts.note: the figure one printed on a calendar marks a particular day

explanation.definitionFit: Each monthly page of a calendar starts with the numeral 1, the opening day.
